(Pkg-293)|190.88|25(2)(d)| The primary function of stator air coolers is to safeguard the health of a generator. They operate as a vital cooling system, actively removing heat generated within the core components – the iron and copper. This heat transfer process relies on circulating air as an intermediary. During operation, the generator's iron and copper components naturally generate heat, and this heat directly transfers from the hot iron and copper to the circulating air that comes in contact with them. The stator air coolers then take over, effectively removing the heat from the warmed air that absorbed it from the generator components. By maintaining this continuous heat removal cycle, the stator air coolers prevent excessive temperature rise within the generator's core, ensuring its optimal performance and longevity. The NJHPS employs a total of 72 stator air coolers distributed across its six generating units.
